minutes.headline: Stormwater task force reworked its slide deck to present neutral funding choices for the town's MS4 compliance to Select Board and FinCom.
minutes.summary: The task force reviewed the stormwater presentation slide by slide ahead of the Select Board and Finance Committee sessions. Members agreed to retitle it around funding mechanisms, drop the tiered fee structure, add an operating-budget-versus-utility comparison, and reconcile revenue and impervious-area figures. One member showed an analysis of fee impact on commercial and residential properties. Next meeting set for the 29th on Zoom.

votes.outcome: passed (all four members answered aye on roll call)

budget_items.what_was_said: The current stormwater line is described as the amount that finally got in, and the MS4-only budget under discussion is much larger.

budget_items.topic: Stormwater operating budget vs current line
budget_items.what_was_said: The DPW director's budget is just under the half-million range, leaving a gap beyond the current line that would come from cuts or an override.
The deck's estimate for stormwater infrastructure value was questioned against a comparison town's higher estimate; members agreed to say 'greater than' a figure.
Bids and estimates for replacing catch basins ranged widely; contractor day rate was also cited.
Chapter 90 historically about a set amount, roughly doubled recently; uncertain year to year and cannot cover big stormwater projects; pavement budget was cut.
A comparison town has a per-unit area and annual fee under a hundred dollars with abatement credits; proposed local fee is based on equivalent residential units.
Dropping tiers yields somewhat more revenue; group agreed to remove the tier structure.
Overhead was recalled as a percentage, earlier figures were higher; later overhead cost mentioned in dollars.

budget_items.topic: Projected fee revenue at ERU rate
budget_items.what_was_said: Table showed revenue above the earlier budget target; 10% allowance for credits and abatements discussed; small residential share of revenue didn't match impervious share.
Sewer minimum quarterly bill cited and non-payment rate discussed for collection analogy.

budget_items.topic: Annual operating budget and one-time equipment
budget_items.what_was_said: Operating budget around a figure with one-time equipment removed; a large earlier total criticized as too big; outsourcing hourly rate vs in-house.
Position split between stormwater and general DPW, with the non-stormwater share falling on the operating budget regardless of funding mechanism.

budget_items.topic: Separate operating override at fall town meeting
budget_items.what_was_said: A different town's large operational override is going before voters; local last override was in 2018.
Analysis showed most non-residential and residential properties would see small percent increases, with a fifth of commercial seeing over a tenth; fee could rise if budget is raised.
A consultant said the draft permit requires replacing a fraction of noncompliant catch basins and annual retrofit projects; one client estimated the replacement cost.
Mailing postcards with QR code reduces printing and mailing costs.

decisions.decision: Retitle the presentation to focus on funding mechanisms for MS4/stormwater compliance rather than assuming a utility.
Agenda topic two to be changed to funding mechanisms; add a slide introducing both options, operating budget first, then utility, then side-by-side comparison.
Infrastructure value to be presented as 'greater than $70 million' with the comparison town cited.
Remove the tiered fee structure from slides and keep the ERU example only; fix example fees to be consistent.
Move the compliance-first slide to the front of the deck and use consistent 'operating budget' wording.
John to reconcile revenue and impervious-area split discrepancies before the presentations.
Change 'stormwater program manager' to 'junior engineer' and note the added 25% of time goes to general DPW work.
Reword straw-poll slide to refer to preferred funding mechanism, not level of support for utility.
Remove the 'fall 2027 present fee structure to select board' timeline item; budget goes to town meeting for approval.
Propose once-a-year billing, with quarterly option considered only if pushed back.
Keep the same presentation for both Select Board and FinCom sessions next week.
Deck revisions to go out about end of day tomorrow; FinCom materials by end of day Monday.
The chair will recuse from the Select Board for the stormwater article and sit with the task force, and will not vote on the recommendation.
Next task force meeting set for the 29th at 7 on Zoom.

what_happened.line: The task force agreed to retitle its stormwater deck around funding mechanisms for MS4 compliance, rather than assuming a utility.
Members voted on nothing but agreed to drop the tiered fee structure and keep only the equivalent-residential-unit example, with example fees made consistent.
The deck will present the operating budget first, then a utility, then a side-by-side comparison, and the straw poll will ask which funding mechanism is preferred.
One member was assigned to reconcile the revenue and impervious-area figures before the Select Board and Finance Committee sessions, which will use the same deck.
The chair will recuse from the Select Board on the stormwater article, sit with the task force and not vote on the recommendation.

why_it_matters: How the town pays for stormwater compliance could land on a tax bill through the operating budget, or on a separate fee, and the task force is shaping the choice residents will be shown.
Funding from the operating budget beyond the current stormwater line would mean cuts elsewhere or an override vote, while a utility fee would be billed by property rather than raised through taxes.
